edu.h: The educational player: listen and watch the song change. Click a part, repeat it with LOOP, follow the bar count.
edu.secret-id.i1: The first 16 bars are only kick and bass: a pure DJ intro. At bar 17 the hi-hats come in, but the main melody is still waiting. A 48-bar intro, 16 + 32.
edu.secret-id.b1: Kick and bass leave in a single bar. Chords and space remain. 16 bars.
edu.secret-id.u1: The highs climb bar by bar; in the last four bars the bass is cut, the tension before the drop. 20 bars.
edu.secret-id.d1: Everything returns: kick, bass and the main melody, the mids 5 dB louder than in the intro. 48 bars of main.
edu.secret-id.b2: The second breakdown, again 16 bars without the kick.
edu.secret-id.u2: A short build-up of 8 bars: the tension peaks faster.
edu.secret-id.d2: The second drop, 32 bars of main. This is where a DJ usually brings in the next song.
edu.secret-id.o1: The outro is the intro in reverse: the melody leaves, kick, bass and hi-hats remain, exactly as in bars 17 to 48. 16 bars to mix out.
edu.i-follow-rivers.v1: The song starts with the voice: the first verse, the story. There's no DJ intro; this is the short version of the song.
edu.i-follow-rivers.p1: The beat stops and the voice climbs towards the chorus. 8 bars.
edu.i-follow-rivers.c1: The chorus: the song's title, the hook. The beat comes back. 8 bars.
edu.i-follow-rivers.n1: 8 bars without the voice: the instrumental part, a pause before the second verse.
edu.i-follow-rivers.v2: The second verse: new words on the same melody. 8 bars.
edu.i-follow-rivers.p2: The pre-chorus, shorter this time: only 4 bars.
edu.i-follow-rivers.c2: The chorus again: the same hook, the same 8 bars.
edu.i-follow-rivers.br: The bridge: the beat stops, only an echo of the hook remains. Once in the song, unlike anything else.
edu.i-follow-rivers.c3: The last chorus, twice: 16 bars. The song ends on its chorus, with no outro; for mixing, pick the extended version.
g.l: A DJ doesn't mix songs, a DJ mixes parts of songs. If you can hear where the intro starts, where the beat breaks and where it comes back, you know when to come in and when to leave. This guide shows it on my demo mix: every example is a real waveform, every part can be played.
g.u.beat: One beat. In house music it's the kick drum: 120 to 125 beats a minute.
g.u.bar: Four beats. The first is the strongest, and everything important starts on it.
g.u.phr: Eight bars, 32 beats. Producers change the song on phrase lines: every 8, 16 or 32 bars something comes in or leaves.
g.u.sec: One or more phrases of the same character: intro, breakdown, chorus. A section lasts 8, 16 or 32 bars, rarely anything in between.
g.wave: Reading the waveform: red is bass and kick, green the mids, blue the highs. When the red disappears, the beat has stopped; when it comes back at full width, that's the drop.
g.i.l: House, organic house, techno, trance, drum and bass: music built around the instruments, not around a singer. It's made for DJs, so its beginnings and endings are simple and easy to mix. If a voice appears, it's usually a short sample used as an instrument. The order is almost always the same: intro, breakdown and build-up, main, breakdown and build-up again, main, outro.
g.i.intro: The start of the song, made for mixing. Often just kick and percussion, then one instrument after another every 8 bars. It lasts 16 or 32 bars.
g.i.intro.w: The waveform is narrow and even, red kicks in a steady row.
g.i.intro.dj: This is where you come in: the new song's intro goes over the outro of the one that's playing.
g.i.break: The beat stops. Kick and bassline drop out; pads, textures, sometimes a voice remain. Room for the dancers to breathe.
g.i.break.w: The waveform narrows suddenly and the red disappears.
g.i.break.dj: Don't leave the song in the middle of a breakdown: the floor is waiting for the drop that comes after it.
g.i.build: The end of the breakdown that rises: snare rolls, a rising noise sweep, a filter opening. Tension before the return.
g.i.build.w: The waveform grows to the right, bar by bar.
g.i.build.dj: Don't bring anything new in here: let the tension reach its peak.
g.i.drop: The moment everything comes back: kick, bassline, the main melody. The first bar of the main part, the moment the dance floor waits for.
g.i.drop.w: Full width and the red come back in a single bar.
g.i.drop.dj: Drop on the drop: bring the other song in exactly on its drop and you lift the room twice.
g.i.main: The meat of the song: everything is in, phrase after phrase, something new every 16 bars. Also called the drop or the groove.
g.i.main.dj: The safest place to mix: there's no voice to clash with another voice.
g.i.outro: The end of the song, the intro in reverse: instruments leave one by one until only the kick and an echo remain.
g.i.outro.w: The waveform thins, the colours fade.
g.i.outro.dj: This is where you leave: the outro and the next song's intro play together for 16 or 32 bars.
g.x1.s: Main, breakdown, build-up, drop, twice. Click a part to hear it in the player.
g.x1.n: In the mix this song's intro ran under the previous song's outro, so the example starts in the main part. The bar counts are measured from the beat analysis.
g.x2.s: Reframing ends, Miss You arrives: outro over intro.
g.x2.n: Reframing's beat stops in its outro; the kick that comes back is the intro of Miss You. The next main part is already the new song.
g.v.l: Pop, vocal house, soul, mantras and kirtan: music built around a singer and a story. You recognise the parts by the voice: the chorus repeats, the verse tells. Different mixing rules apply here, because two voices must never collide.
g.v.intro: The start, before the first voice or with a short lead-in. Short in radio edits, 16 or 32 bars of beat in DJ versions.
g.v.intro.dj: Pick the DJ versions (extended mix): a two-bar radio intro can't be mixed.
g.v.verse: The verse: the singer tells the story. The words don't repeat, but each verse has the same number of bars as the one before.
g.v.verse.dj: Don't cut a verse: a sentence stopped halfway sounds like a mistake.
g.v.pre: A short climb from the verse into the chorus: the energy gathers, the melody rises. Usually 4 or 8 bars.
g.v.pre.dj: The sign that the chorus is a few bars away.
g.v.chorus: The chorus, the hook: the part you remember and sing along to. It almost always carries the song's title and repeats, the same number of bars every time.
g.v.chorus.dj: The easiest place to mix in vocal music; the new song's chorus sits well on the end of the old song's chorus.
g.v.bridge: The bridge: once in a song, different from everything else. It connects the chorus to something else and gives a pause before the last chorus.
g.v.bridge.dj: If it sounds like neither a verse, nor a chorus, nor the end, it's the bridge.
g.v.outro: The end: often a repeated chorus fading away, or a beat without the voice, left for the DJ.
g.v.outro.dj: Leave when the voice is done: two singers at the same time confuse the floor.
g.x3.s: The voice separated from the mix (Demucs) shows where each part is.
g.x3.n: The remix opens with the chorus: the song's title repeated on its own, over a breakdown. Then 8 bars without the voice (a bridge), the verse, the pre-chorus and the full 16-bar chorus. Under the last chorus the next song's beat is already coming in: this is where I left the song, before its bridge and outro.
g.c.i: A whole song on one line: a letter for the part, a number for the bars. Write it on the record sleeve or into the comment field of your DJ software and you know the structure without listening.
g.c.ki: I intro · B breakdown and build-up · M main (drop) · O outro
g.c.kv: I intro · V verse · C chorus · B bridge · O outro
g.c.ex: vo next to a part means there's a voice in it, bt single beats that aren't a full bar.
g.m.i: In instrumental music almost everything can be mixed: intro over outro is the classic, main over main is safe, and a breakdown only if a drop follows it. Count phrases: the new song comes in on the first bar of a phrase, never in the middle.
g.m.v: In vocal music, watch the voice: mix in the intro, the outro and the chorus, never in the middle of a verse. When two songs overlap, only one of them may sing.
g.src: Following the course Instrumental Structure and Vocal-Based Music. The songs in the educational player are from my set; the beat from djay Pro's analysis, the sections from the kick, the frequency bands and the voice separated from the song (Demucs, Whisper).
e.bascut: The bass is cut: the drop is coming.
e.voice: The voice from the first bar.
e.stopv: The beat stops, the voice stays.
e.story: A new verse, the story goes on.
e.echo: An echo of the hook, no beat.
